marks.gloss_en: והדר מייתי לה לערלה פרי פרי מבכורים -- then he brings orla from bikkurim by 'fruit' / 'fruit'
מיתיבי: 'physicians of elil' -- granted for the one who says marteka, that is what is not healable; but for the one who says knife-left flesh, that is healable!
the verse: 'but you are plasterers of lies, you are all physicians of elil' (Job 13:4)
on the verse's alal everyone agrees; they disagree on the mishna's alal
the stam: on the alal of the verse everyone agrees [that it is marteka]

תא שמע: R' Yehuda -- collected alal with an olive-bulk in one place makes one liable, and Rav Huna: when he collected it. Granted for knife-left flesh; but for marteka, what of an olive-bulk? it is mere wood!
R' Yehuda: collected alal, if there is an olive-bulk in one place -- one is liable for it
according to R' Yehuda they do not disagree; they disagree according to the Rabbis -- R' Yochanan: marteka also joins; Reish Lakish: only knife-left flesh, marteka does not join
the stam: according to R' Yehuda they do not disagree; where they disagree is according to the Rabbis
היכי דמי: if he intended [to eat] it, it becomes impure even by itself; if he did not intend it, he nullified it!
one said: he intended part of it
one said: he intended [to eat] part of it
one said: part of it an animal ejected and part a knife
and one said: part of it an animal ejected and part of it a knife ejected
חרטום עץ בעלמא הוא -- the beak is mere wood!
Teharot: the beak becomes impure, imparts impurity and joins
the lower beak
תחתון נמי עץ בעלמא הוא -- the lower one too is mere wood!
the lower part of the upper [beak]
R' Elazar: [the mishna speaks] of the lower beak
R' Yochanan: the mishna's alal is marteka
talons -- R' Elazar: the place embedded in the flesh
horns -- Rav Pappa: at the place where one cuts and blood comes out of them
as seeds, which will not end up with severe impurity, require hechsher (Lev 11:38), so all that will not end up with severe impurity requires hechsher
דתני דבי רבי ישמעאל: וכי יתן מים על זרע ...
'if water be put on seed' (Lev 11:38): as seeds, which will not end up with severe impurity, require hechsher, so all that will not end up with severe impurity requires hechsher
ותניא, אמר רבי יוסי: ... מפני שסופה לטמא טומאה חמורה
R' Yosei: why did they say the carcass of a pure bird requires intention and does not require hechsher?
הכשר למה לי? סופו לטמא טומאה חמורה, וכל שסופו לטמא טומאה חמורה לא בעי הכשר
it will end up imparting severe impurity, and whatever will end up imparting severe impurity does not require hechsher
they teach: [an animal slaughtered by] a Jew in a non-kosher animal or a gentile in a kosher one requires intention [to be food impurity]
